title: Stroke: history or residual deficits
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's past stroke and any residual deficits.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for residual right-sided hemiparesis.

HPI
Pt is an 80-year-old female presenting for evaluation of chronic neurological deficits following a prior ischemic stroke. Pt reports stable functional status. She notes some difficulty with fine motor tasks due to right-sided hemiparesis but continues to perform ADLs with assistance. She remains right-handed. No new complaints of weakness or sensory changes reported since last visit.

Medication List
1. Lisinopril 10mg QD
2. Atorvastatin 20mg QD
3. Aspirin 81mg QD

Vitals
BP: 132/78
HR: 72 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on RA
Ht/Hgb: 34% / 10.2 g/dL
eGFR: 62 mL/min

Review of Systems
Negative for chest pain, SOB, syncope, or focal weakness. No changes in vision or hearing.

Social History
Lives at home with daughter. Retired. No tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History
Mother: Hypertension, Stroke.
Father: Type 2 Diabetes.

Exam
General: Alert, oriented x3, in no acute distress.
Neuro: Cranial nerves II-XII intact. Motor: 4/5 strength in right upper and lower extremities. Decreased sensation in right hand. Pt is right-hand dominant. Gait steady with a cane.
CV: RRR, no murmurs.
Lungs: CTAB.
Skin: Intact, no breakdown.

Assessment
1. Residual right-sided hemiparesis secondary to past ischemic stroke. Pt is currently stable with no signs of progression.

Plan
1. Continue current medications as prescribed.
2. Continue physical therapy 2x/week to maintain mobility and strength.
3. Follow up in 3 months for routine neurological check.

Electronically signed, T. Haddad, NP, 05/14/2026
explanations: Residual hemiparesis after an ischemic stroke, right dominant side: I69.351 (HCC 253).

distractors.why: Check the documented handedness; when it is not documented, the right side is dominant and the left side non-dominant.
Residual hemiparesis is documented: code the sequela (I69.35-, HCC 253), not Z86.73.
